newsitem.title: USA: Rep. Kennedy seeks support for new oil reserve.
newsitem.headline: Rep. Kennedy seeks support for new oil reserve.

text.p: U.S. Rep. Joseph Kennedy is seeking support from other lawmakers for a bill to set up a petroleum products reserve, and ease the rules for drawing down oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, according to a letter released Tuesday.

In a January 8 letter to other House members, the Massachusetts Democrat said he would introduce legislation "to address the problems consumers have experienced this winter from supply shortage scares to price spikes in the volatile heating oil, natural gas, and propane markets."
"As you probably know, industry reserves are at an all-time low and consumers are paying on average 25 percent more for their heating fuels this year compared to last winter," the letter said.
Kennedy pressed Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary last fall to step into the market to build up heating oil stocks to avert a jump in prices this winter.
O'Leary refused, saying any action by the government would be counterproductive and that the administration had no authority to use SPR oil to prevent a heating oil price rise.

Kennedy said he would propose to build a regional products reserve, change the law governing use of the SPR to allow the administration to swap SPR crude for heating oil and redefine emergency use of the SPR to include regional, not just national, crises.
He also proposed to establish a program to encourage consumers to fill their heating oil tanks in the summer to be prepared before the heating season.
